title: Evoked potentials
what: The doctor shows you pictures, plays sounds, or gives weak pulses to your arm or leg. Electrodes on your head record how fast the signal reaches the brain.
why: For problems with vision, hearing, or feeling, for a possible nervous system disease, or to check the nerves.
duration: usually 30 to 90 minutes; the report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you wear glasses or contact lenses

prepare.title: Hair
prepare.text: Wash your hair the day before, with no oil or hairspray.

prepare.title: Glasses
prepare.text: Bring your glasses or contact lenses, if you wear them.

prepare.title: Wellbeing
prepare.text: Get a good night's sleep. You can eat in the morning.

steps: Electrodes are put on your head, and sometimes on an arm or leg
For vision: you look at a screen with a checkerboard
For hearing: you wear headphones with clicking sounds
For feeling: weak pulses are given to an arm or leg
You need to sit still and pay attention
feel: The pictures and sounds do not hurt
The pulses feel like light tingling or a finger twitching
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days

faq.a: They are weak and feel like tingling. The strength is set so it is bearable.

faq.q: Can I wear glasses during the test?
faq.a: Yes, and you should. Bring your own glasses or lenses.

reminders.text: Evoked potentials test tomorrow. Wash your hair with no oil or hairspray. Bring your glasses, if you wear them.
